title: Syncopation (1942): the New York jam session sequence
summary: The jam session with Krupa, Venuti and others was filmed in New York, and Barnet doubts Rex Stewart was in that segment because of Hollywood prejudice.

blocks.x: And the last listing of your films is, 'Syncopation.'

Oral History
Interview with Charlie Barnet by Patricia Willard
Reel 4

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 847-5395
P R O C E E D I N G S

At the end of the last reel we were about to talk about the last film listed in 'Jazz in the Movies,' and that is, 'Syncopation,' 1942, directed by William Dieterle, a musical romance tracing in fictional form the development of jazz from 1906. Many musicians are featured including Benny Goodman, Charlie Barnet, Joe Venuti, Gene Krupa, Harry James, Rex Stewart, Alvino Rey, Jack Jenney, Connie Boswell, and the Hall Johnson Choir. Some sound track ghosting was done by Bunny Berygigan for Jackie Cooper, and by Stan Wrightsmann for Bonita Granville. Lee Keith Stevens provided several songs. What do you remember about that?

Well, the basic group that you mentioned, we did the recording of that in New York. The picture was actually made in California, but the jam session sequence, which I presume is what this is all about, with Gene and all the people you mentioned there, we did that over at 20th Century Studios on 11th Avenue in New York. And this of course was sent out to Hollywood and incorporated in the picture. Because there were no dramatic roles involved in this at all.
I see. Was Rex Stewart's presence there a problem? Apparently he was on screen from the way this reads. Is that right?
I don't believe that Rex was in this
segment that was filmed in New York.
I don't recall him being there.
You mean he could have been by himself or something?

There may have been another -- I haven't seen the picture in so long I've almost forgotten it. But there may have been another scene, possibly in conjunction with the Hall Johnson Choir, that Rex was in. Because I'm quite sure that at this time the same prejudice existed in the movies. They were too scared of what would happen when the thing played Dallas and Atlanta and who knows where else. But Rex was definitely not with the group in New York. The group in New York was Joe Venuti and Krupa, and well, the rest of them that you named there, and I'm sure that Rex wasn't there.
